papers.summary: Let $q\equiv 3\bmod 4$ be a prime power and let $K$ be a finite separable extension of the field of rational functions $\mathbb F_q(t)$, with constant field $\mathbb F_q$. We show that $\mathbb F_q[t]$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb F_q(t)$ and that the latter is Diophantine in $K$. We deduce from work of Demeyer that $K$ has the DPRM property: Diophantine sets over $K$ are the same as listable sets.
papers.title: Diophantine sets over global function fields

papers.summary: Physics simulation outputs increasingly come from solvers that no expert inspects, such as third-party packages in automated pipelines, programs written by large language models (LLMs), and learned surrogates. In earlier work on cardiac pulsed field ablation, we proposed that solvers return a certificate with their answers. The certificate consists of an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current, and a small independent checker turns it into guaranteed error bounds against a written specification of the physics. Here, the same checker verifies the outputs of other solvers on the same problem. Specifically, FEniCSx computes both fields and receives the same bounds as our own solver. Five plausible bugs in a correct solver, one of them about 0.2% from the true impedance, all converge and pass a grid convergence study, yet the certificate rejects or refutes all five. Of three solvers written by LLMs, one is correct and certified to 0.1%, and one never solves the equation but converges. Neural networks that predict the coefficients of a reduced basis emit admissible fields and receive valid per-prediction bounds, at most 0.0021% wide inside their training range and 0.3-25% wide outside it, where 90% conformal intervals cover none of 14 tests. Untuned Fourier neural operators with free nodal outputs receive valid but uninformative bounds. On a uniform grid, interpolation onto the certificate grid limits them, and on the certificate grid, thin cells turn small nodal errors into large energy errors. Energy-norm training narrows the certified interval tenfold, and projecting the nodal-loss outputs onto the reduced basis narrows it by two to four orders of magnitude, still uninformative. The guarantee concerns the stated model and holds for any output, wherever its input lies. It is informative only when the output is accurate in energy on a grid that resolves the problem.
papers.title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates

papers.summary: We study the Bergman projection $P_ω$ on a radial tree with respect to weighted harmonic Bergman spaces $A^p_ω$, where $ω$ is a positive radial weight. We prove that for all such weights and $1<p<\infty $, the Bergman projection $P_ω$ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $A^p_ω$ and $L^\infty \to \mathcal{B} $, where $\mathcal{B} $ is the Bloch space of the tree. We also provide a characterization of the weights $ω$ for which the positive Bergman projection $P_ω^+ $ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $L^p(ω) $. Finally, in the appendix, we provide an elementary proof of the characterization of the weights $Ω\in L^1(\mathbb{D}) $ for which the Bergman projection from $L^p(Ω) $ to the holomorphic Bergman space $A^p_Ω(\mathbb{D}) $.
papers.title: Weighted Bergman projection in radial trees

papers.summary: Let $L_1, L_2\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be lattices of the same volume and let $D_1, D_2$ be two bounded fundamental domains for $L_1, L_2$. We show that there is a measurable common tile for $L_1$ and $L_2$ contained in $D_1+D_2$. The main tool is a result of Bowen, Kun and Sabok (2021) which shows how to obtain a measurable perfect matching given a fractional perfect matching in hyperfinite graphings.
papers.title: Common tiles from fractional tiles for two lattices

papers.summary: We study the quantale, or multiplicative lattice, of additive submonoids of an arbitrary ring, with particular focus on the question of which properties of the ring can be recovered from it. We show that this quantale, unlike the better-known quantale of ideals, captures significant information about the cardinality, characteristic, and center of the ring. Certain rings, such as non-prime finite fields, torsion-free rings, and those with characteristic 2, are completely determined by their submonoid quantales. We also discuss various other subobject quantales one can associate to a (semi)ring.
papers.title: Quantales Arising From Rings

papers.summary: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.
papers.title: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process

papers.summary: This paper proposes and investigates a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem representing the interaction between incompressible flows and porous media flows through the Beavers-Joseph-Saffman interface conditions. A fully discrete numerical scheme has been proposed and analyzed employing backward Euler temporal discretization and a locally conservative LDG scheme for the space discretization. The well-posedness of the numerical scheme has been obtained under a small data condition. Optimal a priori error estimates have been proven in the energy norm, as well as the L2-norm for t>0. Numerical experiments ensure the efficiency of the theoretical results
papers.title: A locally conservative LDG method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem

papers.summary: How far apart, on average, can $n$ points in a set $A$ be? As $n\to\infty$ the answer is the $\textit{maximal energy}$ $M^{+}(A)$, the largest possible value of $\mathbb{E}|X-Y|$ when $X$ and $Y$ are independent random points of $A$ with a common distribution. If the distribution is allowed to carry negative mass, we obtain a second constant $M(A)\ge M^{+}(A)$. It is often far easier to compute: when a signed equilibrium measure exists, it is characterized by a $\textit{linear}$ potential equation, whereas the positive problem must also locate the support of the mass. This paper asks when positivity matters, that is, when $M^{+}(A)<M(A)$. For polygons and polyhedra the extremal mass sits on the vertices and closed forms abound. Even so, every hollow convex polygon has $M^{+}<M$, and a simple kite shows how a vertex can be forced out of the support. For smooth curves and surfaces the answer depends on the shape. Circles and spheres have $M^{+}=M$. The ellipse $x^2+4y^2=4$ has $M^{+}=M$ numerically, and we give its value to 50 digits. The ellipses $x^2+9y^2=9$ and $x^2+25y^2=25$ have $M^{+}<M$ numerically, with gaps in the support. For the ellipsoid $10x^2+15y^2+12z^2=15$, studied by Larcher, Schmid and Wolf, we compute 50 digits of $M$ and give strong numerical evidence that $M^{+}<M$. The extremal measure vanishes on two caps around the ends of the shortest axis. Proofs and numerical methods are collected in appendices.
papers.title: When Positivity Matters: Maximal Distance Integrals on Curves and Surfaces

papers.summary: Agentic AI tools have recently had success in mathematical reasoning. Both general purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, and specialized mathematics agents such as Aristotle, have been used for formalizing mathematical problems such as Fermat's last theorem, Erdős problems and several IMO level math problems. However, much of these efforts are concentrated in the pure mathematics domain, which benefits from relatively self-contained theorem statements, fixed mathematical representation and extensive support in existing formal libraries. Applied mathematics, on the other hand, presents additional challenges because the source may describe a computational procedure or modeling transformation rather than a declarative theorem. In this work, we present a systematic study of AI-assisted auto-formalization for scientific computing (SC), a domain in applied mathematics central to U.S. Department of Energy applications. Through case studies spanning hierarchical abstraction layers in SC software stack, we evaluate not only whether AI agents can complete numerical proofs, but also where and why they fail across the stack. Our primary contribution is a cross-layer taxonomy of failure modes and an analysis of the form of expert feedback required at each layer to recover mathematical soundness. From these observations, we derive a workflow for recurring proof patterns and practical guidance for using AI agents while preserving mathematical soundness. Our results characterize both the practical value and the current limitations of AI-assisted formalization for trustworthy scientific computing.
papers.title: AI-Assisted Auto-formalization for Trustworthy Scientific Computing: Case Studies and Lessons Learned

papers.summary: FP64 emulation on integer tensor units now ships in cuBLAS and GEMMul8, and each emulated matrix product can be checked against an accuracy grade. We ask if a routine built from such products inherits their accuracy, and show that blocked triangular inversion, the core of LAPACK's inverse of a symmetric positive definite matrix, does not. Under fixed-precision emulation every product passes the grade-B error bound of Demmel et al., yet the inverse errs at 7.1e-2, against 2.0e-15 natively. The matrices are well conditioned after diagonal scaling, but the scaling spans 64 binades. The cause is one product, T = X22 L21, whose summed index carries both the diagonal scaling and its inverse, which a grade-B bound does not absorb. Computing those products natively restores native accuracy; leaving any one of them emulated does not. The pattern holds on four GPUs, and on real covariance matrices the fixed-precision routes lose up to about four orders of accuracy. Equilibration, a solve-based association and cuBLAS's automatic dynamic precision avoid the loss, and an exact error recurrence audits a completed run. On an RTX 4090 the fastest accurate emulated inversion takes 0.40 of cuSOLVER's time. Where each product's scaling falls decides if per-product accuracy carries over to a composite routine, and that is what builders of emulated libraries need to check.
papers.title: Accurate Products, Inaccurate Inverse: Emulated FP64 BLAS in Blocked Triangular Inversion

papers.summary: For a positive semidefinite matrix $X$, let $μ_k(X)$ be the minimum of the least eigenvalues of its principal submatrices of order $k$. For positive semidefinite $A,B$ of order $n$, we prove \[ μ_{i+j-1}(A\circ B)\geqμ_i(A)μ_j(B), \qquad i,j\in\{1,2,\dots,n\},\quad i+j-1\leq n, \] and characterize equality when the right-hand side is positive. The resulting symmetric least-eigenvalue bound \[ λ_{\min}(A\circ B)\geq \max_{1\leq i\leq n}μ_i(A)μ_{n-i+1}(B) \] recovers the classical Schur lower bounds at endpoint choices and can be exact even when both factors are singular. It is incomparable with the projection bound from a recent companion paper, and combining the two bounds can improve on both. The proof combines a spectral minorant of $B$ whose diagonal entries are at least $μ_j(B)$ with the projection inequality underlying the companion bound. Multifactor and Khatri--Rao consequences are also given.
papers.title: A symmetric eigenvalue lower bound for Hadamard products

papers.summary: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calderón-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.
papers.title: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity

papers.summary: Let $κ$ be $λ$-supercompact for a regular $λ>κ$. We show that if $λ$ is not the successor of a singular of cofinality below $κ$, $\diamondsuit(S^λ_{\geqκ})$ implies that every ${<}κ$-strategically closed forcing of size at most $λ$ is a projection of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing. We show that the situation for successors of singulars of small cofinality is independent. Finally, we provide more limitations about the class of $κ$-distributive projections of the $λ$-supercompact Prikry forcing and give examples of $κ$-distributive forcings of size $λ$ which cannot be projections of this forcing.
papers.title: On Cohen Generic Sets in Supercompact Prikry Extensions

papers.summary: It is shown that the equivalence relation on Cohen generic reals over a countable model of set theory, where two are equivalent if they produce the same generic extension, is hyperfinite, answering a question of the author. The proof uses asymptotic separation and is a digestion of an argument originally produced by GPT-6.
papers.title: Equivalence of Cohen generics is hyperfinite

papers.summary: We investigate the relative geometry of annihilators of zero divisors in the real sedenion algebra. Each nonzero zero divisor has a four-dimensional annihilator, whose geometry is associated with an axis in the imaginary octonions. For two prescribed axes separated by an angle $θ$, we establish the exact range of principal angles between their annihilators. The four principal cosines are necessarily $(p,p,q,q)$, where $\cos^2(θ/2)\leq p\leq\cos(θ/2)$ and $0\leq q\leq p$, and every admissible pair is realizable. We further derive an explicit quadratic formula for the principal cosines of any specified pair using two invariants of the associated quaternionic frames. A continuous deformation demonstrates that neither the axis angle nor the underlying quaternion subalgebras together determine the annihilator angles. Finally, we relate these results to the least singular subspaces of sedenion left multiplication through Euclidean projection onto the zero-divisor cone.
papers.title: Principal angles between annihilators of real sedenion zero divisors

papers.summary: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the André-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.
papers.title: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman

papers.summary: Let A be a noetherian positively graded algebra. We investigate several weighted numerical homological regularities: weighted CM-regularity, weighted Tor-regularity (Ext-regularity), and weighted Ex-regularity, defined in terms of the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of canonical complexes associated with graded A-modules. Introduced by Kirkman, Won, and Zhang, weighted regularities provide finite invariants even when their unweighted counterparts are infinite. Through parametrized degree reweightings, they unify classical homological invariants, including unweighted numerical regularities, sup, inf, depth, projective dimension, and local cohomology dimension. This framework clarifies the behavior of homological regularities under degree shifts and reveals intrinsic relationships among these invariants, particularly those involving the a-invariant. We establish several inequalities and equalities relating these weighted regularities to the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of derived Hom and derived tensor complexes. These results recover their unweighted counterparts and yield new relations involving the a-invariant for a fixed weight. Some of these results generalize the inequalities of Kirkman-Won-Zhang between weighted CM-regularity and Tor-regularity by allowing the weight to range over the entire plane R^2. We also give conditions under which these inequalities become equalities, thereby answering a question posed by Kirkman-Won-Zhang. We use weighted AS-regularity to study the Artin-Schelter regularity of A. Under mild conditions, we prove that the weighted AS-regularity of A vanishes if and only if A is an N-graded AS-regular algebra. This generalizes an unweighted result of the present authors and a weighted result of Kirkman, Won, and Zhang.
papers.title: Weighted Numerical Homological Regularities over Positively Graded Algebras

papers.summary: AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, for which homological integrals are defined, form a broad class of (infinite-dimensional) Hopf algebras. We establish an $S^4$ formula for left AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, thereby generalizing Radford's $S^4$ formula for finite-dimensional Hopf algebras and refining the formula of Brown and Zhang by identifying a group-like conjugating element in the Hopf algebra $H$. Our approach is to endow the space of left homological integrals $\int^{\ell}_H$ with a canonical right $H^*$-module structure compatible with its natural right $H$-action. If the $H^*$-action is rational, then $\int^{\ell}_H$ carries a canonical $(\mathrm{id}_H,S^4)$-twisted right-left Yetter--Drinfeld module structure. The right $H$-action and left $H$-coaction on this one-dimensional space determine a character and a group-like element in $H$, respectively; the twisted Yetter--Drinfeld compatibility condition then yields the $S^4$ formula. The $H^*$-action on $\int^{\ell}_H$ is rational if either the coradical of $H$ is coreflexive or the trivial left module $\Bbbk$ admits a finitely generated projective resolution. In particular, the latter condition holds when $H$ is left noetherian. We also establish a corresponding result for right AS-co-Gorenstein Hopf algebras with coreflexive coradical. As applications, we use the $S^4$ formula to study the bijectivity of the antipode and derive explicit finite-order bounds when $H$ is module-finite and faithfully flat over a central right coideal subalgebra, or finitely cogenerated and faithfully coflat over a cocentral quotient.
papers.title: The Fourth-Power Formula for the Antipode in AS-Gorenstein Hopf Algebras

papers.summary: Let $(E, P)$, $(E', P')$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{C}$ with marked $p$-torsion points; a marked isogeny is an isogeny sending $P$ to $P'$. We show the marked isogeny relation is interpretable in $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and has strict infinite chains. It follows that $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property, which confirms a special case of the stable fields conjecture.
papers.title: $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property
